Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a critical darling, earning praise as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!**—Cole Escola's absurdist farce reimagining Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist—proves that irreverent comedy continues to find enthusiastic audiences.

The rest of the top ten showcases Broadway's range, from the satirical punch of **The Book of Mormon** and **Chicago**'s cynical celebrity commentary to the visual spectacle of **The Lion King** and **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child**. Whether you're drawn to revolutionary classics, imaginative new works, or spectacular revivals, March 2026 presents an exceptional opportunity to experience Broadway at its most varied and accomplished.

This reimagined production proves that even beloved classics can find fresh resonance with bold directorial choices, though the approach doesn't win over every traditionalist.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as perhaps the most significant artistic achievement from this group—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally received its long-overdue Broadway debut in a stellar revival that demonstrates the work's enduring examination of race, power, and identity within the military. With the strongest review count at 29 notices, it clearly captured substantial critical attention.

The season also brought more divisive fare: **My Name is Lucy Barton** showcases Laura Linney's luminous solo performance in an intimate literary adaptation, while **West Side Story** arrives in Ivo van Hove's characteristically radical reimagining, splitting critics between those who embrace its bold vision and those who resist its departures from tradition.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five shows, the 2020 season—though abbreviated—delivered a solid mix of classical revivals and important dramatic work. best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—a season cut short by unprecedented circumstances, yet one that managed to deliver several productions still worth examining today.

Among the five plays from that truncated year, **Les Misérables** stands out with the strongest critical reception. This grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre earns praise for its fresh approach to the classic material, though the reimagining doesn't win over all traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** marks a significant milestone: Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally reached Broadway in a revival that critics widely celebrate for its stellar performances and the continued relevance of its examination of race and identity in America.

The remaining productions showcase Broadway's range, from intimate character study to broad comedy to radical reinterpretation. **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides opinion—Laura Linney's performance garners universal acclaim in this solo adaptation of Elizabeth Strout's novel, even as critics debate the theatrical merits of the adaptation itself. **Grand Horizons** offers more conventional pleasures as a boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Meanwhile, Ivo van Hove's **West Side Story** proves the most polarizing entry, with its bold directorial choices and video design elements earning both passionate defenders and harsh detractors.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the 2020 class reflects a year of artistic ambition meeting real-world constraint. For theatergoers interested in this particular moment in Broadway history, these reviews offer insight into which productions have left the most lasting impact.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2021 represent a pivotal moment in theater history—the industry's triumphant return following the pandemic shutdown. These productions, now five years into their legacy, showcase remarkable artistic ambition and innovation that helped redefine what Broadway could be.

The ten highest-rated plays and musicals from 2021 average an impressive 81/100 critical score, reflecting a season marked by bold experimentation and powerful storytelling. Leading the pack is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's extraordinary lip-sync performance to a real interview recording—a technique that critics found both unsettling and unforgettable.

Close behind are two theatrical institutions taking vastly different approaches: **The Phantom of the Opera**, Andrew Lloyd Webber's enduring spectacle that proved melodrama and chandelier-drops never go out of style, and **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**, Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining that transformed the August Wilson Theatre into a pre-war Berlin nightclub, earning widespread acclaim for its environmental staging.

The season also saw powerful solo performances in **Lackawanna Blues** and urgent contemporary work like **Pass Over**, which made history as Broadway's first show back after the shutdown. Gender-swapped revivals (**Company**), pop-infused historical reimaginings (**SIX**), and sweeping financial epics (**The Lehman Trilogy**) rounded out a diverse slate that balanced commercial appeal with artistic risk-taking.

Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting old favorites, this guide highlights the productions that defined Broadway's resilient comeback.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable period that brought both innovative new voices and powerful revivals to the stage. The shows that debuted that year continue to resonate with audiences, earning an impressive average critic score of 83/100 across our featured productions.

Leading the pack is *Kimberly Akimbo*, the quirky musical that critics consistently describe as a near-perfect achievement, masterfully balancing comedy with profound emotional depth. Close behind, two productions share the spotlight: *Into the Woods*, a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as both celebration and tribute to the late composer, and *A Strange Loop*, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical that broke new ground with its brazenly original approach to storytelling.

The 2022 season proved particularly notable for its embrace of Pulitzer Prize-winning works, with multiple honored plays making their Broadway debuts or returns. From Tom Stoppard's deeply personal *Leopoldstadt* to revivals of Suzan-Lori Parks' *Topdog/Underdog* and Paula Vogel's *How I Learned to Drive*, the season demonstrated Broadway's commitment to substantive, challenging drama. The year also showcased diverse theatrical forms, from Mike Birbiglia's solo storytelling in *The Old Man & The Pool* to Jordan E. Cooper's audacious sketch-comedy satire *Ain't No Mo'*.

What unites these productions is their willingness to tackle difficult subjects—mortality, identity, historical trauma, and human connection—with intelligence, craft, and emotional honesty. Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting old favorites, this collection represents some of the finest theatrical work of the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the plays that opened on Broadway in 2023 continue to demonstrate the remarkable artistic vitality of that theatrical season. With an average critic score of 82/100 across our top ten selections, these productions represent a diverse range of voices and styles—from classic revivals to bold new works.

**Merrily We Roll Along** stands as the highest-rated production, with Maria Friedman's revival earning an 85/100 score and finally giving Stephen Sondheim's once-maligned musical the recognition it deserves. Sharing that top rating is **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, a West End transfer that surprises critics with its technical ambition and theatrical sophistication beyond mere franchise extension. Close behind, **Appropriate** earns an 83/100 for Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama, anchored by Sarah Paulson's acclaimed performance.

The 2023 season proved particularly strong for revivals with contemporary resonance. **Purlie Victorious** and **Parade** both score 82/100, bringing mid-century works back to Broadway with urgent relevance for modern audiences. Meanwhile, new voices flourished: **Fat Ham**, James Ijames's Pulitzer Prize-winning riff on *Hamlet*, brings fresh perspective to classic material, while **Stereophonic** earns praise for its immersive portrayal of the creative process.

The range extends from Alex Edelman's solo show **Just for Us** to the music-driven spectacle of **Buena Vista Social Club**, proving that Broadway's play category encompasses vastly different theatrical experiences. Whether you're seeking intimate storytelling, large-scale revivals, or innovative new works, these 2023 productions offer compelling reasons to experience theatre at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As of March 2026, the Broadway shows that debuted in 2024 continue to demonstrate exceptional staying power, with several productions still captivating audiences more than a year after their openings. This collection of ten standout productions—averaging an impressive 83/100 critic score—represents one of the strongest theatrical seasons in recent memory, spanning inventive new musicals, bold comedic experiments, and meticulously crafted revivals.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's critically acclaimed drama about a 1970s rock band, which earns near-universal praise for its authentic portrayal of the creative process and theatrical ambition. Close behind, **Operation Mincemeat** proves that grassroots sensations can translate to Broadway success, with critics celebrating its inventive energy and ensemble work. **Maybe Happy Ending**, a robot love story that critics call one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, rounds out the top tier with its unexpected emotional depth.

The season's diversity is particularly notable: Cole Escola's irreverent **Oh, Mary!** reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist to riotous effect, while Audra McDonald brings fresh interpretation to the iconic Mama Rose in a handsome **Gypsy** revival. More intimate fare like **Mary Jane**—Amy Herzog's understated drama about maternal devotion—balances the spectacle of lavish productions like **Oliver!**

From Justin Peck's dance-driven **Illinoise** to Shaina Taub's educational yet entertaining **Suffs**, these productions showcase Broadway's remarkable range in storytelling approaches and artistic ambition. Whether you're seeking emotional depth, comedic brilliance, or innovative stagecraft, these 2024 productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As spring arrives on Broadway, the 2025 season continues to resonate with audiences through a diverse slate of productions that spans intimate dramas, ambitious revivals, and imaginative new works. This month's top ten plays average an impressive 84/100 from critics, reflecting a particularly strong year for theatrical storytelling.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread acclaim for transforming Arthur Miller's classic into a visceral examination of moral responsibility. The production's emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work demonstrate how bold directorial choices can illuminate timeless material for contemporary audiences.

Musical theater also claims significant critical attention. **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** returns for its 20th anniversary with a revival that critics describe as joyous and perfectly timed, while the family-friendly **Paddington The Musical** enchants reviewers with its remarkably lifelike bear puppet—a genuine theatrical marvel that pushes the boundaries of stagecraft.

The season's range extends from Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English**, which sensitively explores language and identity, to David Yazbek's darkly comic **Dead Outlaw**, chronicling the bizarre afterlife of outlaw Elmer McCurdy. Meanwhile, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins delivers another sharp family drama with **Purpose**, and **Ragtime** returns with renewed relevance, anchored by Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance.

Whether drawn to classic American drama reimagined for modern sensibilities, inventive new musicals, or award-winning contemporary plays, theatergoers will find March 2026 offers an abundance of critically acclaimed options worth exploring.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a notably lean opening schedule for new Broadway plays, with just one production making its debut this month. While the limited roster reflects the challenging economics facing straight plays on Broadway, the sole entry demonstrates the enduring appeal of well-crafted psychological drama.

**Bug** stands as the month's singular offering, marking the long-awaited Broadway premiere of Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller. With a solid critic score of 74/100 across 35 reviews, the production earns mostly positive notices for its intense exploration of paranoia and delusion. Originally produced by Chicago's Red Orchid Theatre three decades ago, the play arrives on Broadway with renewed relevance, its themes of conspiracy and fractured reality resonating in contemporary discourse. Critics particularly praise the production's claustrophobic staging and committed performances, though some note the material's deliberately unsettling nature may not appeal to all theatergoers.

The sparse March schedule underscores a broader trend in commercial theater, where plays increasingly struggle to secure Broadway berths amid rising production costs and risk-averse producers. That **Bug** makes it to the Great White Way at all speaks to both the strength of Letts' reputation—bolstered by his Pulitzer Prize-winning **August: Osage County**—and the theater community's ongoing commitment to provocative, challenging work.

For audiences seeking substantive dramatic fare this month, **Bug** offers a compelling if confronting option that showcases the raw power of theatrical storytelling. Those planning their spring theater calendar should consider catching this production while monitoring announcements for upcoming play openings in the months ahead.
